newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish wheat area loses to barley, no output fall.
newsitem.headline: Turkish wheat area loses to barley, no output fall.

text.p: A small portion of Turkey's total wheat lands has been lost to barley farming in 1997/98 but will not reduce wheat output this crop year, a senior farm official said on Wednesday.
"Some farmers in southern regions have turned to barley growing this year although they were farming wheat on their lands before," said the official, who asked not to be identified.
"But the area lost to barley is not so big as to have much impact on the usual total wheat area of eight to nine million hectares," he told Reuters.
He did not give any figure for the reduction in wheat area but agricultural analysts and some farmer groups put it at up to 500,000 hectares (ha).
In 1996/97, Turkey produced about 16.5 million tonnes of wheat from about nine million hectares -- about one-third of the country's total arable land. Land sown to barley is about 3.5 million ha.
"That does not take into account farming carried out on marginal lands like pastures and steep slopes. Farmers produce wheat in about one million hectares of such land," the official said.
He said many farmers in southern areas opted for barley because it is not affected by the pests which damaging wheat in those areas in the spring.
The government sprays some one million ha of wheat in southern regions, especially Cukurova, to fight bug damage.
Another agricultural official said the area lost to barley would be offset by effective seeding, use of pesticides and good weather.
"All measures have been taken to prevent any drop in wheat output due to the reduction," he said.
Both officials said it was too early to make any crop estimates but added factors affecting grain production had been favourable since the sowings in autumn.
"The main factor in grain production is rains in spring, especially in April and May," said one official. "The rains have been very good all over Turkey so far."
The officials said the first official crop estimate would be carried out by the ministry and the state grain board (TMO) in late May after the spring rains.
"With the assumption that all factors carry on to May as they have been so far, there should be no reason for a crop less than that realised last year," the official said.

He said an International Grain Council (IGC) estimate that Turkey could produce 16.8 million tonnes of wheat and eight million tonnes of barley in 1997/98 could be realised. --Ankara newsroom, 90-312-4462940
